product_from_film: Pear presents a social prediction-market account that finds markets across services and lets users follow others’ trades.
explains_well: A news question becomes a Yes/No market, a cross-service search and a social trade card before a portfolio result.
unclear: Routing quality, odds, settlement, eligibility, fees and actual returns are not verified.
scenario: See SpaceX news, select a Yes outcome, find a market, share a position and view a closed position.
product_clear_basis: A Yes/No market appears at 7s, followed by Finding best markets between Pear and named market services at 10–12s.

scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 13–22s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 31–38.8s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: News discovery → outcome selection → market finding → social trade → event/value montage → closed position → waitlist.
A runner and Pear logo establish a character and brand; the product task emerges only after he reaches the news screens.
Prediction trading is visible at 7s, cross-service finding by 12s and social function around 18s.
Outcome selection enlarges, service marks change, social card scales up and a green value line rises over rocket footage. Exact timing and paths unverified.
Real-world-looking phone use alternates with clean UI; the news/rocket theme connects the market question with the later value montage.
Night reflections and warm interiors contrast with pale interface cards and a bright sky ending.
Market question and Yes/No prices are readable focal points; social details and final portfolio entries are more dense.
The inspected ASR draft provides partial script-role support; recognition limits are recorded in A02. Audible voice characteristics and delivery remain unchecked.

categories.finding: Silent sequence shows a news-linked prediction, market choice and social position. The relation between displayed contract price and later dollar values is unexplained.
Enlarged Yes choice and social card focus attention on one action at a time before the wider event montage.
Several product functions and market-success cues fit into 39s. One complete trade with defined values could reduce ambiguity.
The news question becomes a position and closed-state display, but the event resolution and financial calculation are not clearly explained.
Excited phone users and rising rocket/value imagery may imply opportunity and reward; audience response is unmeasured.
The SpaceX IPO question and returning initial user connect the story across interfaces and other users.
The film shows selection, service marks, social trade and closed-position states. Actual routing, returns, settlement and platform access are untested.
Pear appears on the runner, routing card and waitlist close; the social-market card adds product-specific context.
A clear outcome-resolution screen could replace some rocket imagery and explain the result more directly.

lessons.keep: Carry one news question and the same user through selection to a visible result.
